original_card.question: Can one measured replay bottleneck be sped up without dropping coverage?
methods: Profile one isolated replay and optimize the measured bottleneck.
Design source-bound reuse with explicit dependency invalidation and negative controls.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Report before/after wall time on the same fixture, retained checks and invalidation behavior.

first_step.inspect: Resolve the current selected review, separate complex/ordinary BIT/admitted BIT/outer budgets, and compare the card against live handoffs before starting. Historical ceilings require exact source/model equivalence.
first_step.scope: Source-binding orientation only; not a scientific replay or all-size proof. Materialize selected inputs if this checkout is sparse.

original_card.first_experiment: Measure one unchanged fixture, preserve check coverage, and test one optimization with invalidation controls.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Faster trustworthy replays increase review throughput and let mechanism candidates be checked sooner.
allowed_variations: Profile one stage or design one source-bound cache boundary.
scope_change_triggers: Skipping coverage or comparing different fixtures to claim speedup.

actual_scope: Reduce complete research-package source-validation peak allocation with an exact bounded-memory working-file comparison.
scope_change_reason: The mathematical card allocation is changed to a distinct verifier-engineering bottleneck found in the shared metadata/pin validator. This changes implementation rather than auditing predecessor mathematics.
bottleneck_link: Large live source archives currently allocate a second full working-file buffer during exact pin validation; reducing it lowers the memory needed to reproduce research packages.
stop_rule: Ship the first verified reduction in complete validator peak traced allocation, with identical full validation output and rejecting controls; retain any measured timing regression.
evidence: Seven normal/optimized contract tests and five alternating fresh-process pairs on complete physical-gaussian-core metadata/pin validation. Raw measured samples and source hashes are in BENCHMARK.json.
author: Nick Petalas
ai_assistance: Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

open_questions.question: Can the retained pinned Git blob also be streamed without weakening provenance and cleanup checks?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The comparison now uses at most a 1 MiB data buffer, but the existing Git reader still retains a whole blob.
open_questions.first_step: Design a bounded chunk protocol with exact size, blob identity, SHA256, final status and reader-cleanup contracts before benchmarking it.
open_questions.blocked_by: The current git_blobs public contract yields complete bytes; changing it affects several consumers.

throughput_checkpoint: One writer, one existing isolated worktree. Implement one helper and caller substitution, prove exact comparison, run contracts, then measure the complete metadata/pin consumer serially. No delegated work or scientific replay.
